compiled_state.description:
## Context

Bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events breaks the event store's append-only union invariant. Independently valid stale clones can then produce delete/modify conflicts instead of reconverging without history loss.

Gerrit change 989, commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d, removed queue and digest pruning and added a real two-clone regression proving both histories survive and merge cleanly. That was the required correctness and recovery fix.

Removing pruning creates a deliberate long-term retention problem. Each successful enrichment cycle normally appends ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST events; retries or claim races can append more. At the 2026-07-27 measurement, the live tickets tree contained 1,198 such files totaling about 1.23 MB: roughly 5.5% of tracker files and 0.5% of tracker bytes.

Queue reduction reads accumulated per-ticket event history, pending-work discovery scans every ticket directory, and latest-digest lookup enumerates the ticket directory. Without retention, live file/inode counts and these O(history) scans grow linearly, increasing clone, checkout, index, merge-tree, and operational costs. The former deletion scheme bounded only the live tree; deleted blobs remained in earlier Git history, so it never truly bounded repository storage.

Existing follow-up task 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d records the initial retention design work. This epic preserves the broader architectural context and is intentionally out of scope for the current session.

## Long-term objective

Design and land merge-safe retention, compaction, or archival semantics that bound hot/live tracker cost while preserving cross-clone convergence, crash recovery, auditability, and every independently committed event or a lossless compacted representation. Physical deletion or rename of committed UUID events is not an acceptable solution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current queue and digest growth rates and read/clone/index costs are measured with deterministic benchmarks.
- [ ] The chosen design bounds hot/live event lookup and working-tree growth without rewriting or deleting independently committed UUID events.
- [ ] Real two-clone stale-history tests prove independent retention operations reconverge cleanly and preserve all logical state.
- [ ] Crash recovery, claim leasing, latest-digest selection, auditability, and migration/rollback behavior are documented and tested.
- [ ] Operational rollout includes monitoring and a safe migration for existing unbounded histories.
- [ ] The relationship between live-tree retention and Git object/history storage is documented so the design does not claim storage reclamation it does not provide.

## Related evidence

- Closed root-cause bug: 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282
- Existing retention-design task: 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d
- Correctness fix: Gerrit change 989 / commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d
compiled_state.title: Bound tracker growth without deleting committed event history
